name: Test Equipment

claims.claim_text: When Hewlett-Packard split in 1999, the computer and printer business retained the HP name and the test and measurement business was renamed Agilent, so instruments carrying decades of HP brand equity had to be rebranded.
claims.quote_verbatim: I was devastated that when the computer division of HP, you know, the printers and all that got the HP name and the test gear, you know, was forced to change to Agilent.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A common hobbyist pattern in the used-instrument trade is to buy multimeters and other instruments cheaply on eBay, refurbish them, and resell them, cycling through a large number of units over the years.
claims.quote_verbatim: I used to buy and sell test equipment on eBay all the time just because I enjoyed it.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Transistor Types and Where To Get Electronic Gear

claims.claim_text: Access to surplus test equipment is strongly regional: the United States has a deep surplus market where a lab of nominally high list-price instruments can be assembled for a tiny fraction of that, while Australia has almost no equivalent supply.
claims.quote_verbatim: I live in Australia. I don't get access to all this cool surplus test gear like you guys in the US have.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: RF and microwave instrumentation shown by exhibitors at conferences such as the International Microwave Symposium is typically six-figure equipment, with individual instruments rarely worth less than 100,000 dollars.
claims.quote_verbatim: none of that test equipment is worth less than $100,000, it seems like
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: Analog circuit designers of the 1960s and 1970s worked without simulators, computers or even pocket calculators, relying on slide rules and on far more limited instrumentation than is now routine.
claims.quote_verbatim: They didn't have simulators. They didn't have computers. They didn't have calculators even.
claims.episode_title: Apple HQ and Vintage Arcade Games - The Mothership Manifesto

claims.claim_text: Good Will Instek is a Taiwanese instrument maker whose mid-range oscilloscopes and function generators are sold under the Goodwill or Instek brand depending on the country of sale.
claims.quote_verbatim: They make some, you know, reasonably, reasonably good quality middle of the range test gear.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Alan Yates - Recondite Radiation Raconteur

claims.claim_text: Taiwanese mid-range instrument makers found themselves undercut by as much as 50 percent by mainland Chinese competitors selling copied products, despite already having a low-cost manufacturing base.
claims.quote_verbatim: they're being undercut by at least, by up to 50%
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Alan Yates - Recondite Radiation Raconteur

claims.claim_text: In a mature production line the marginal cost of testing can approach zero once the automated test equipment is fully depreciated, at which point line uptime rather than test cost governs the economics.
claims.quote_verbatim: The good thing is testing equipment that we've had here is paid for. So, you know, the cost is basically zero and you put it on there and it's, it's all, it's all automated equipment.
claims.speaker: John Edmond
claims.episode_title: An Interview with John Edmond - Luciferous LED Lucubrator

claims.claim_text: Surplus electronics dealers differ in what they stock: some are large undifferentiated piles of mixed junk, while smaller curated dealers concentrate on industrial gear and instruments that stand a reasonable chance of still working.
claims.quote_verbatim: CNH is more test equipment that might have a possibility of actually working.

claims.claim_text: All Electronics, a United States catalogue component supplier, also operates a walk-in retail store in Van Nuys, California, a fact not widely known among its mail-order customers.
claims.quote_verbatim: we also went to All Electronics, which is a catalog supplier in the U.S. I don't think very many people know that they have a retail store, but they actually have a retail store in Van Nuys

claims.claim_text: A working definition of test equipment is any instrument used to measure other equipment, which places even inexpensive educational instruments in the category when they are used to debug hardware.
claims.quote_verbatim: Equipment that measures other equipment is usually test equipment.
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ian Daniher - Nascent Nonolith Numquid

claims.claim_text: Low-cost exploratory instruments intended for learning are not substitutes for production instrumentation, which must do things like curve-trace transistors coming off a line to confirm they meet specification.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's not the sort of thing that you would go to curve trace your transistors coming off the line to make sure they meet spec.
claims.speaker: Ian Danaher
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ian Daniher - Nascent Nonolith Numquid

claims.claim_text: Practising RF engineering requires a large quantity of expensive instrumentation, which is a structural reason engineers in the field gravitate to employers who already own the gear rather than working from home labs.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you want to be an RF engineer, you got to have equipment, right? Oh, yeah. It helps. Lots of it. And it's all really expensive, right?
claims.speaker: Tom LeMense
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Tom LeMense - Cacaesthestic Chronometric Carriwitchet

claims.claim_text: Home RF benches tend to be assembled from vintage instruments whose frequency coverage and noise performance are inadequate for modern work on Bluetooth or Wi-Fi.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's all pretty vintage and certainly nothing I'd want to try to work on like Bluetooth or Wi-Fi or something like that with
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Tom LeMense - Cacaesthestic Chronometric Carriwitchet

claims.claim_text: Work that depends on shared instrumentation, particularly RF measurement, argues for co-locating a team rather than distributing it, because the equipment cannot be duplicated at every remote desk.
claims.quote_verbatim: especially with test equipment and things like that, it's, it's really, uh, it's really helpful to be in the same place
claims.speaker: Matt Ettus
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Matt Ettus - Quality Quadrature Quidam

claims.claim_text: High-end instruments are built in low volume and therefore receive far less user-interface engineering than mass-market low-cost instruments, whose large user base generates constant usability feedback.
claims.quote_verbatim: the high-cost ones are really low volume. So you've got to figure that they don't get as much optimization as like a, you know, a low-cost Rigol
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Ceramic capacitors & High end scopes - Kempt Kickstarter Kakorrhaphiophobia

claims.claim_text: A high-end oscilloscope is designed primarily for automated compliance analysis of serial standards such as SATA rather than simply displaying a waveform, which explains its feature set and its interface complexity.
claims.quote_verbatim: this oscilloscope's not designed just to get a waveform on the screen. It's designed to do automated analysis of serial, you know, signals
claims.episode_title: Ceramic capacitors & High end scopes - Kempt Kickstarter Kakorrhaphiophobia

claims.claim_text: Instruments needed only occasionally are better rented than bought, and companies developing high-speed products often find test equipment consuming a large share of the research and development budget.
claims.quote_verbatim: when you need it, you can rent it. That's the real thing.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Ceramic capacitors & High end scopes - Kempt Kickstarter Kakorrhaphiophobia

claims.claim_text: In smaller markets distributors carry little or no stock of obscure or high-end instruments and their demonstration loan units are often already out with another customer, which forces buyers into rental.
claims.quote_verbatim: not many of the suppliers carry stock, right, of, you know, either an obscure bit of test gear or a high-end bit
claims.episode_title: Ceramic capacitors & High end scopes - Kempt Kickstarter Kakorrhaphiophobia

claims.claim_text: A common failure of equipment rental is that a unit taken for a few days stays on the books for years, because nobody revisits the rental once the immediate need has passed.
claims.quote_verbatim: So you go to these rental companies thinking, oh, yeah, we'll just rent it for a couple of days. And then two years later, right, someone from accounts comes in and goes, do we still need this bit of gear?
claims.episode_title: Ceramic capacitors & High end scopes - Kempt Kickstarter Kakorrhaphiophobia

claims.claim_text: Non-recurring engineering costs such as tooling and test equipment are significant on a hardware programme, but staff cost usually dominates, which is why firms under pressure shed people before they shed instruments.
claims.quote_verbatim: NRE kind of stuff, like molds and, you know, like, for early-run protos is a significant cost and test equipment is a big cost
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Ceramic capacitors & High end scopes - Kempt Kickstarter Kakorrhaphiophobia

claims.claim_text: Experienced production technicians carry empirical fault knowledge about specific boards, so consulting them before building simulations saves time that theorising alone will waste.
claims.quote_verbatim: Get to know your technicians. Get to know anyone who's good with that stuff because you will look like an idiot.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Mars, Makerbot & Power Outages - Reprobate Replicator Replication

claims.claim_text: Knowledge of how production test gear works and how to maintain it often ends up concentrated in a single employee, which is a maintenance risk for the organisation and a weekend burden for that person.
claims.quote_verbatim: I've been the only one in the company who knew how all the production test gear worked and how to maintain it.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Mars, Makerbot & Power Outages - Reprobate Replicator Replication

claims.claim_text: Instrument makers deliberately withhold features from lower tiers to protect very expensive high-end products, adding secondary conveniences instead of the performance that would cannibalise the flagship line.
claims.quote_verbatim: If you're selling a scope, you know, a hundred giga sample scope for, you know, a hundred grand or whatever it is, you don't want to just go and give that all away. So you just throw in other bells and whistles.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: FPGA, Xess, 32 Bit - Quirky Qualitative Questions

claims.claim_text: Measurements for which no commercial instrument exists require building custom test gear, as in a purpose-built drift counter used to track oscillator frequency drift over time.
claims.quote_verbatim: because there's no real instrument that allows you to do it. So you have to roll your own, you know. You've got to build your own test gear to do that sort of thing.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: FPGA, Xess, 32 Bit - Quirky Qualitative Questions

claims.claim_text: The absence of any commercial instrument capable of a measurement is a useful signal that the work has crossed from engineering into science.
claims.quote_verbatim: You know that you're entering the science realm outside of the engineering realm. If there's no test gear yet.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: FPGA, Xess, 32 Bit - Quirky Qualitative Questions

claims.claim_text: Acquiring an oscilloscope is a turning point for a self-taught engineer because seeing signals in the time domain converts abstract circuit behaviour into something observable.
claims.quote_verbatim: being able to visualize signals I think in a time domain. Oh it's huge.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: FPGA, Xess, 32 Bit - Quirky Qualitative Questions

claims.claim_text: Calibration laboratories must hold environmental conditions inside defined limits to issue certification, typically a temperature window of about 5 degrees Celsius and relative humidity in the region of 30 to 80 percent.
claims.quote_verbatim: It has to be within a 5 degree C window.
claims.episode_title: Melbourne, Hackerspace & Calibration - Vacuuous Vortex Verification

claims.claim_text: Instruments returned for calibration from harsh industrial sites are often found coated internally with contamination, so environment of use is a factor in an instrument's condition and drift.
claims.quote_verbatim: test gear coming back from, like, really rough environments and just being, like, completely coated inside
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Melbourne, Hackerspace & Calibration - Vacuuous Vortex Verification

claims.claim_text: Incumbent instrument makers repeat a disruption pattern in which they retreat toward ever more expensive high-margin products and abandon the low end, leaving that segment to cheaper entrants.
claims.quote_verbatim: companies end up wanting to move to higher and higher levels of, you know, expensive stuff, right? So they don't want to sell you transistors.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Intel, EPA & Brown Field - Google's Ground Gurgitation

claims.claim_text: Agilent's decision to separate its electronic measurement business, which became Keysight, followed from test and measurement being a lower-margin segment than its rapidly growing life sciences division.
claims.quote_verbatim: We can't have this low-margin, boring test equipment holding us back.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Agilent's New Name, Molex's New Owner and PCB artwork - Nonsensical Naming Neolatry

claims.claim_text: A standalone test and measurement company can serve instrument users better than a division inside a conglomerate, because its chief executive's attention is on measurement rather than on a larger unrelated business.
claims.quote_verbatim: if it's just a test and measurement company then, and you have a CEO who's focused on test and measurement, then yeah, okay, he cares about test and measurement
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Agilent's New Name, Molex's New Owner and PCB artwork - Nonsensical Naming Neolatry

claims.claim_text: Oscilloscope performance is limited by the weakest subsystem: an expensive high-bandwidth front end delivers little if the trigger system has excessive jitter, since rare events cannot be reliably captured.
claims.quote_verbatim: You can have a $50,000 fantastic front end on the, you know, on a 50 gig scope. But if your trigger system's got, you know, jitter from here to Timbuktu, then you ain't going to be able to do anything.

claims.claim_text: A survey of three decades of electronics magazine advertising shows the entry-level oscilloscope price point holding steady at roughly 700 to 800 dollars, a level maintained deliberately so that cheap models do not undercut the tiers above.
claims.quote_verbatim: even over 30 years, the entry level price was, you know, around that seven, $800 figure
claims.episode_title: Someone is watching...we think - Horme Hostility Hypochondriac

claims.claim_text: A standardised open hardware platform with interchangeable analog front ends can act as a general-purpose instrument chassis, letting analog designers contribute front ends while software work is shared.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's like you tack a front end under this thing and it's basically whatever test equipment you need it to be now
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Mike Ossmann Returns! - Planetic Portalab Packaging

claims.claim_text: Constrained low-cost tools such as a bus analyser or basic logic tool cover roughly 80 percent of users' needs, and buying a multi-thousand-dollar instrument is best deferred until a specific job actually requires it.
claims.quote_verbatim: You know, they're constrained in what they can do. But oftentimes, it covers 80% of the people that are going to use it in the first place, right?
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: The 2014 Maker Faire Show - Traveling Technology Trangam

claims.claim_text: The instrument market changed sharply over the late 2000s and early 2010s, to the point where a 500-dollar oscilloscope offers capability that previously required far more expensive equipment.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can buy a 500 buck scope and wow, you know, the shit it can do is phenomenal
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: The 2014 Maker Faire Show - Traveling Technology Trangam

claims.claim_text: Contrary to the assumption that rising signal speeds would push everyone to higher bandwidth, the bulk of instrument users remain below 100 MHz while a smaller group needs six-and-a-half, seven-and-a-half and eight-and-a-half digit multimeters, so vendors must serve a broadening base and a rising top end at once.
claims.quote_verbatim: the masses are still, you know, sub 100 megahertz
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: The 2014 Maker Faire Show - Traveling Technology Trangam

claims.claim_text: Persisting with an inadequate low-end instrument can consume far more effort than reaching for the right instrument at the outset, even though the struggle has some teaching value.
claims.quote_verbatim: So it took you seven videos to dick around to get to that point where you use the tool you should have used to start with.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Tesla, Checklists and Bullies - Emerging External Eupsychics

claims.claim_text: Hameg is a European instrument brand with little presence in the United States but a near-leading position in Europe, particularly in the education market and in low-cost affordable instruments.
claims.quote_verbatim: they're not huge name in the West, but in Europe, they're, you know, almost number one
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Solar Factories and HVDC Lines - Pollent Power Pushing

claims.claim_text: Well-equipped labs typically contain many instruments that are used only a small fraction of the time, which is a reason to weigh occasional-use purchases against rental or borrowing.
claims.quote_verbatim: isn't everyone's lab filled with test gear that they're only going to use 1% of the time?
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Last Minute Decisions - Obdurate Onepercenter Obstacles

claims.claim_text: Engineers who produce public measurement content while employed by a research laboratory can keep the two strictly separate by owning all the instruments used for the public work, avoiding any claim on the employer's equipment or results.
claims.quote_verbatim: All my test gear is completely separate. All my own test gear, nothing to do with Bell Labs at all.
claims.speaker: Shahriar Shahramian
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Shahriar from The Signal Path - Quisquous Quivering Quadripole

claims.claim_text: The International Microwave Symposium carries a large industry exhibition showing state-of-the-art instruments from every manufacturer, whereas circuit and ASIC conferences have little physical hardware to demonstrate.
claims.quote_verbatim: at IMS conference, there is an enormous industry show, which I think you would absolutely love. Because all this state-of-the-art instrument from every manufacturer is there.
claims.speaker: Shahriar Shahramian
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Shahriar from The Signal Path - Quisquous Quivering Quadripole

claims.claim_text: Electronics magazines of earlier decades were filled with test equipment construction projects because affordable commercial instruments did not exist; a digital storage oscilloscope kit sold in the thousands simply because a ready-made DSO could not be bought.
claims.quote_verbatim: I sold thousands of my digital storage scope kit because back then you couldn't buy a digital storage scope so you built your own
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: MightyHohm For The Holidays - Kaiser Keyzer's Kits

claims.claim_text: Building common bench instruments from scratch is rarely economic today, since a conventional 30 volt 3 amp linear bench supply can be bought for around 50 dollars, leaving DIY justified only for niche requirements.
claims.quote_verbatim: 30 volt 3 amp linear bench supply you can get them for like 50 bucks on ebay
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: MightyHohm For The Holidays - Kaiser Keyzer's Kits

claims.claim_text: National Instruments' VirtualBench combines several instruments in one box at a price around two thousand dollars, which places it above the reach of most hobby and educational buyers.
claims.quote_verbatim: Which I want to love except it's two grand
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Can't We All Just Get Arduino? - Tardiloquent Trademark Tirade

claims.claim_text: Instrument design has trended toward consolidation, with mixed-domain oscilloscopes and similar products absorbing functions that were once separate boxes.
claims.quote_verbatim: everybody's just consolidating. It's just like, you just keep pouring more and more features into something.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: The Art Of Staying Interested In Electronics - Exponible Electronics Ennui

claims.claim_text: Production test systems commonly remain on obsolete operating systems such as Windows 3.11 or DOS for decades, because the equipment still produces working product and there is no forcing reason to revalidate a new platform.
claims.quote_verbatim: i know that there's production test gear which i've designed um that is still running windows 3.11 right and dos stuff
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Radio regulations in the United States and across Europe contain exceptions for test equipment, which is how a broadband transmitter covering roughly 1 MHz to 6 GHz can legally be sold when it would not be permitted as a consumer device.
claims.quote_verbatim: in most countries, definitely in the US and throughout Europe, there are exceptions for test equipment
claims.speaker: Michael Ossman
claims.episode_title: A Security Update with Michael Ossmann

claims.claim_text: Semiconductor parts are usually obsoleted only when something physical forces it, such as a fab closing or the production test equipment for that part becoming unusable, at which point customers are offered a last-time buy.
claims.quote_verbatim: if the fab is shutting down or, you know, the test equipment can no longer be used or something, then sometimes you have to say, sorry, guys. You know, last buys.
claims.speaker: Dafydd Roche

claims.claim_text: Some instrument vendors police the secondhand and clone market by searching eBay listings and filing reports to have them removed, an approach that affects what used buyers can find.
claims.quote_verbatim: Searching eBay and putting in reports and getting people flagged and taken down
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A typical progression for a beginner's bench runs from multimeters and a simple kit oscilloscope to a two-channel oscilloscope and a signal analyser, driven by work such as PWM debugging that a single-channel instrument cannot resolve.
claims.quote_verbatim: I have multimeters and a little kit oscilloscope I built myself, but I've started doing some more advanced projects like with PWM and stuff, and I find myself more and more needing like things like a two-channel oscilloscope

claims.claim_text: Reaching 50 MHz of analog bandwidth with off-the-shelf parts is difficult at a low price point, which is the central engineering constraint on inexpensive USB and student oscilloscopes.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's like hitting 50 megahertz bandwidth is not easy with off-the-shelf parts, especially at a low cost point
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Clint Cole of Digilent

claims.claim_text: Digilent's later USB instrument work targeted 250 MHz of analog bandwidth while holding roughly the same price bracket as its earlier lower-bandwidth products.
claims.quote_verbatim: The product we're working with on paper now will offer 250 megahertz analog bandwidth and try to be in the same ballpark from a pricing perspective as well.
claims.speaker: Clint Cole
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Clint Cole of Digilent

claims.claim_text: Engineers who travel frequently need instrumentation that is not heavy and bench-based, which is the design driver behind small USB-host-powered oscilloscopes and analysers.
claims.quote_verbatim: how do you move away from test gear that's very heavy and bench-based?
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Clint Cole of Digilent

claims.claim_text: Grouping production measurement data by fixture, chamber or operator exposes systematic offsets, such as one chamber consistently reading higher, that would never be found by looking at aggregate pass or fail rates.
claims.quote_verbatim: you group by a chamber and like chamber one is always much higher, right? You start to actually map the chambers against one another
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: Gauge repeatability and reproducibility studies are worth doing religiously on factory test fixtures as a process control discipline, but they must not replace first checking that the equipment is connected, in calibration and physically sound.
claims.quote_verbatim: if your test equipment is broken, or it's like, let's say you have like a cow stickers off, right? It's out of cow. Or maybe there's like a loose, there's a loose wire or something hanging. Then you can end up spending weeks collecting all this gauge R&R data.
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: Buying instruments can become a substitute for building anything with them, so the purchase should be tied to a specific project rather than pursued as an end in itself.
claims.quote_verbatim: But buying test equipment can also be its own end, you know.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Designers of high-end instruments routinely reject integrated single-chip signal-chain solutions in favour of discrete implementations, because instrument specifications are hard requirements that a general-purpose integrated part cannot be trimmed to meet.
claims.quote_verbatim: any kind of integrated solution, we always said, no, no thanks. You know, because so much of it was that's very specific, you know, need this spec, need that spec.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: All-in-one instruments such as the National Instruments VirtualBench, priced around 5,000 dollars, target academic benches that need adequate acquisition rather than standards-class accuracy and cannot house a full set of separate instruments.
claims.quote_verbatim: they don't necessarily need, you know, standards class instruments. They just need acquisition
claims.speaker: David Ledger

claims.claim_text: Hewlett-Packard's founding product, made in the Palo Alto garage that anchors the Silicon Valley startup story, was a piece of test equipment rather than a computing product.
claims.quote_verbatim: their first product, um, 200 day, 200 was a piece of testing equipment
claims.speaker: Jason Huggins

claims.claim_text: Paying for instruments whose problem is already solved in software, such as a logic analyser with a well-designed capture and decode interface, buys back engineering time even though the hardware itself is expensive.
claims.quote_verbatim: That's like a logic analyzer with like a really intuitive interface. That's a solved problem now.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Instrument user interfaces have historically lagged behind other product categories, which is part of why engineers still favour physical knobs over menu-driven front panels on bench equipment.
claims.quote_verbatim: I think test equipment. And really just electronics in general. Has not done the whole UI piece.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Production throughput is capped by the number of test stands available, since each unit occupies a stand for the duration of its test, which is the economic argument for built-in self-test.
claims.quote_verbatim: so there's a throughput limit there right you know right how many each one needs a new test stand and doing its own thing right
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: In shared lab space, marking an instrument with a prominent fault label is an effective way to stop it being borrowed and to keep a known-good reference instrument available.
claims.quote_verbatim: you put a big red sticker on it. Saying. You know. Magic smoke escaped or faulty. Or something like that. And then nobody's going to borrow it.

claims.claim_text: Test equipment predating the 1960s is marked in kilocycles and megacycles rather than kilohertz and megahertz, a unit convention that can confuse users of vintage instruments.
claims.quote_verbatim: the test equipment in my lab is all like pre-1960s stuff. So it's in kilo megacycles, so it can be confusing.
claims.speaker: Greg Charvat
claims.episode_title: Gregory Charvat and Three New Companies

claims.claim_text: Used instruments bought from another mains region are often not switchable between supply voltages and require modification at the printed circuit board level, a hidden cost of importing secondhand equipment.
claims.quote_verbatim: buying used test gear on eBay and stuff like that is a pain in the butt because a lot of test gear cannot be switched or it has to be modified at the PCB level
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Tektronix in its classic era was vertically integrated to an unusual degree, manufacturing its own cathode ray tubes and supplying the silver solder needed to work on the ceramic terminal strips inside its instruments.
claims.quote_verbatim: they built CRTs in-house
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: Instruments from the 1960s and 1970s were simpler in construction than modern equivalents, so opening one exposes the design decisions and manufacturing process in a way that a current instrument does not.
claims.quote_verbatim: You know, test equipment was simpler back then.
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: High-speed production test equipment is often designed in-house to test subassemblies on the factory floor before final assembly, as with audio modules verified before being fitted into greeting cards.
claims.quote_verbatim: I designed all the high-speed production test equipment that was used on the factory floor to test the greeting card modules before they went into the cards.
claims.speaker: Julia Truchsess

claims.claim_text: Hardware security and protocol testing has shifted from proprietary add-on modules bought for oscilloscopes to open-source tools with Python interfaces, which makes automated and scripted testing accessible without instrument-vendor software.
claims.quote_verbatim: it was more about like these modules that you had to buy for scopes and other physical hardware

claims.claim_text: Small self-contained instruments such as thermocouple data loggers now make continuous retroactive measurement of physical variables cheap, replacing the guesswork that previously accompanied intermittent faults.
claims.quote_verbatim: I can go online and buy a little gizmo with a thermocouple and have an accurate log of my fuel temperature dating back a week retroactively.
claims.speaker: Travis Goodspeed

claims.claim_text: A first oscilloscope should be a known-working unit, even a low-end one, because repairing a second, broken instrument requires a trusted reference to measure against.
claims.quote_verbatim: I think your first scope should be a working scope, maybe a low end working scope. And then you use that to, then you buy your second scope is broken
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Refurbished instrument dealers test what they sell and typically charge about double the price of an as-is private seller, which is the price of removing the risk that the unit is faulty.
claims.quote_verbatim: you're buying it from one of the refurbished test equipment sellers and they will test it. You can be pretty confident, right? If they sell it, but you're going to pay a premium, like a real, like a double what you'd pay for just some individual person selling their instrument as is
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Because bench instruments carry comprehensive built-in self-test, a unit that powers up and passes self-test can be judged 80 to 90 percent likely to be usable, which is the practical screen for a used purchase.
claims.quote_verbatim: the good thing about these instruments is that they, they do have comprehensive self-test built in. So if it boots up and passes the self-test, then, you know, you can, you can be reasonably 80, 90% confident.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The phrase pulled from a working environment is unreliable when it comes from an individual seller, whereas instruments liquidated in bulk by an auction house after a lab or factory closure are near-certain to have been in service.
claims.quote_verbatim: don't, don't trust an individual seller on eBay when they say pulled from working environment
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Instruments sold by auction when an entire factory shuts down carry near-certain confidence of being functional, because they were part of a running production environment rather than an individual's shelf stock.
claims.quote_verbatim: when an entire factory shuts down, then yeah, you know, you're almost like 99% confident that suck is going to work
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Many mainstream instruments now expose Python control libraries, including Rigol oscilloscopes and the Saleae logic analyser, which allows instrumentation to be driven from a continuous integration harness rather than by hand.
claims.quote_verbatim: I believe a lot of the raggle scopes have a Python interface. Oh, really? The Salyer logic analyzer also has a Python library for automation.
claims.speaker: Jonathan Georgino

claims.claim_text: Bringing an instrument into a lecture and showing the mathematics being applied to a real measurement, such as an FFT displayed on a spectrum instrument, makes the theory concrete for students who learn from evidence.
claims.quote_verbatim: if they would pull a piece of test equipment into the room when they're showing you the math
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Hands-on use of an instrument builds intuition and mental models that theory alone does not produce, because the operator can vary a parameter and immediately observe the effect.
claims.quote_verbatim: having hands on with the test equipment and like seeing what happens as you change things
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: The cost of an instrument is usually set by the frequency range required rather than by any general need for the most expensive model, so specifying the frequency span honestly is the main lever on price.
claims.quote_verbatim: you don't have to get the most expensive gear. Um, I just got it more expensive because of the, the frequency range I wanted to play in.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: High-end instruments hold substantial value even when faulty, with broken examples of expensive equipment routinely selling for thousands of dollars, so repair-for-profit at the top of the market requires real capital.
claims.quote_verbatim: I search for these on eBay myself so I can do repair videos. I can tell you they're, they're thousands of dollars for a broken one.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Measurement above roughly 3.2 GHz sits beyond the price most engineers will pay for instrumentation, which limits characterisation work at those frequencies to laboratories with vector network analysers.
claims.quote_verbatim: 3.2 gigahertz, I think is, is, is well beyond the range of what most people want to pay for, for test equipment
claims.speaker: Nash Reilly

claims.claim_text: Modern embedded development often needs only a debugger and a known-good board rather than a large test setup, because contemporary instruments are small, comparatively inexpensive and very capable.
claims.quote_verbatim: we also have access to test equipment today, which is small, relatively inexpensive, and insanely powerful
claims.speaker: Jack Ganssle

claims.claim_text: Ease of hardware modification depends heavily on whether a board exposes labelled test points; some game controller boards provide clearly labelled test pads while others route button contacts as carbon pads on a printed silkscreen circuit that offers nothing to probe or solder to.
claims.quote_verbatim: The only contacts for the buttons are carbon, are carbon pads connected to a silkscreen circuit.
claims.speaker: Ben Heck

claims.claim_text: When a target board is hostile to probing, a third-party equivalent product may be far more tractable, as with a Hori game controller that exposes large labelled test pads.
claims.quote_verbatim: So what I did was I found like this third party controller from a company called Hori and you open it up and it's beautiful. There's big, giant test pads and they're all labeled.
claims.speaker: Ben Heck

claims.claim_text: A durable arbitrage exists in used instruments because buyers in some countries will not risk overseas purchases, so an importer who takes that risk, repairs and cleans the unit, and resells locally can realise around three times the purchase price.
claims.quote_verbatim: I'll buy a test gear from the US and then I'll like get it imported here and then I'll either fix it or clean it up and, and test it out. And then I'd re sell it here for like three, three times what I paid for it.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: At very high data rates small impedance discontinuities accumulate quickly and erode link performance, so installed high-speed infrastructure must be measured rather than assumed to meet the rate it was specified for.
claims.quote_verbatim: little discontinuities, little badnesses stack up so fast at these super high speeds that you can give up performance so fast
claims.speaker: Joel Dunsmore

claims.claim_text: Being able to walk up to an unfamiliar instrument and navigate its menus is a distinct professional skill, complementary to having a small set of personally owned tools used for every job.
claims.quote_verbatim: the presence of mind to be able to walk up to a couple different types of test equipment. Maybe you don't own it, but maybe you, you know, you can navigate menus
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Entering the low end of the instrument market is difficult because the product must ship with a deliberately constrained feature set while competing against established Chinese manufacturers who have already reduced the function to an ASIC.
claims.quote_verbatim: The low end is tough because you're usually playing with a constrained feature set.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: The value in a modern logic analyser lies in its software rather than its FPGA and front-end silicon, which is why a vendor differentiating on user interface can move up market and raise prices.
claims.quote_verbatim: You're paying for the software development.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Precision instruments carry their specifications in their component selection: a single precision resistor can cost four dollars in volume against roughly twelve dollars at single-piece price, so unit economics at low volume can consume most of the margin.
claims.quote_verbatim: Heck, one single resistor on there is four bucks, right?
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Open-source precision instrument designs are frequently rebuilt with lower-precision components, and the resulting units do not meet the original specification even though the schematic is identical.
claims.quote_verbatim: they put lower precision parts on it and it's not the same spec
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Selling a precision instrument to a stated specification requires custom-built test gear to verify each individual unit, and traceability back to a national standard adds further cost to the product.
claims.quote_verbatim: then I've got custom built test gear to actually test each one, you know, and guarantee that's within specification
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Credible independent product testing requires major capital infrastructure, including RF anechoic chambers, acoustic chambers and dedicated power supply test benches, plus engineers hired specifically to run them.
claims.quote_verbatim: they're going to install all sorts of test gear from RF and echoic chambers to acoustic chambers
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Entire categories of instruments exist that are made and sold only inside domestic markets such as China and South Korea, including meters that cannot be bought elsewhere.
claims.quote_verbatim: There's meters that you can, that you can only buy in China, for example.
claims.speaker: Ben Jordan
claims.episode_title: Publicly Traded Hobby with Ben Jordan

claims.claim_text: Calibration and functional test equipment is not part of a normal contract manufacturer's capability, so a product requiring per-unit calibration obliges its designer to supply and maintain that equipment at the CM.
claims.quote_verbatim: a huge part is making sure that it is working correctly and calibrated. So that's expensive equipment that is not part of a normal CM.
claims.speaker: Matt Liberty
claims.episode_title: The Joulescope Upgrade with Matt Liberty

claims.claim_text: Repairing older instruments teaches how instruments are designed, because earlier equipment solves the same measurement problems from a different angle than a modern instrument that hides the method behind software.
claims.quote_verbatim: this stuff, much like repairing old equipment, sort of forces you to learn how equipment works
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: A large modern oscilloscope needed only for a single project is better rented than bought, since the capital outlay cannot be justified by occasional use.
claims.quote_verbatim: that's the kind of thing where you can rent it if it's something that you're needing for a specific project
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: The HP 8753 is regarded as the category leader among comparatively low-cost vector network analysers, and studying such category-defining instruments reveals the measurement philosophy behind them.
claims.quote_verbatim: kind of like how the 8753, like a category leader in like kind of lowish cost VNAs
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: Stanford Research Systems instruments hold their resale value unusually well because the company still builds the same designs decades later, uses through-hole construction, and publishes service manuals, all of which keep old units repairable.
claims.quote_verbatim: they still make them and they still make the same design that they made 20 years ago
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: Public attention to a particular vintage instrument model measurably raises its price on the used market, so buyers of niche gear compete with the visibility of the model itself.
claims.quote_verbatim: we are driving up the price of used test equipment
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: Owning a second identical instrument gives a benchmark to compare against while modifying or repairing the first, which is the practical way to confirm that a modification improved rather than degraded performance.
claims.quote_verbatim: when you've got a second unit to like compare against and do things, it's just so handy
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Buyers in geographically isolated markets must import faulty and used instruments from the United States at shipping costs that can reach around 500 dollars per unit, which changes what is worth repairing.
claims.quote_verbatim: we have to import it from the U S it's, you know, and it costs like $500 shipping
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Repairing test equipment is an effective way to learn both electronics design and instrument design, but it has become genuinely hard because instruments now 40 years old have no factory parts support left.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can't call up tektronics and get parts for it anymore which is like a huge problem
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: Vintage instrument repair in the 2020s spans a much larger technology gap than earlier restoration work, because a great deal of surviving laboratory equipment is around forty years old and built with parts and processes no longer in production.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's now 2024 and a lot of this equipment is like you know 40 years old so I mean it's that's a long time to try to be keeping things alive
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: When a repair requires fabricating an unobtainable part, cutting a batch of ten to thirty costs little more than cutting one on a laser cutter, and the surplus can be sold to other restorers to offset the cost of the hobby.
claims.quote_verbatim: a lot of times it's easier to just make 10 or 20 or 30 parts
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: Vintage oscilloscopes use a rear fan for cooling with a foam filter that prevents dust, dirt and hair being drawn inside, and replacing a perished filter is a routine part of restoring one.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's the little foam thing that goes in the back of the scope that keeps dust and dirt and hair from getting into the scope you know because it has a fan on the back
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: The TekScopes groups.io mailing list is the principal community for vintage Tektronix instrument repair and is notably more active than the equivalent HP and Agilent list, and the Tektronix community also maintains a museum for its vintage equipment.
claims.quote_verbatim: this one I posted to the tech scopes mailing list which is very active that's a Google group yeah or sorry groups IO and that like anybody who's repairing tech equipment is on that list
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: A working test equipment collection accumulates duplicates and project-specific instruments that outlive their purpose, and periodically moving those on keeps the bench usable.
claims.quote_verbatim: I've got things that I bought for a project 10 years ago that I don't need anymore
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: sigrok is an open-source driver layer providing a common interface to a very wide range of oscilloscopes, multimeters and logic analysers, including Bluetooth-connected handheld meters, with separate graphical front ends built on top of it.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's basically an open source universal interface to almost every test equipment on the market.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A common bench layout convention places less frequently used instruments on higher shelves and keeps daily-use instruments at eye or hand level.
claims.quote_verbatim: I tend to put my less used stuff higher up.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Suspending an oscilloscope beneath a shelf, alongside the bench lighting, recovers bench area in a small workspace while keeping the display in view.
claims.quote_verbatim: I actually ended up zip tying my scope underneath the shelves where the lighting was, too. And that actually works really great.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Mounting a source measure unit on a bracket at the back of the bench so its terminals sit at board level shortens the lead path from instrument to device under test.
claims.quote_verbatim: build a bracket and have it mounted to the back of the bench so that then your probes are plugged basically at the same level as your board
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Individual instrument collections can reach industrial scale, with one documented inventory listing 88 multimeters, 38 oscilloscopes, 11 logic analysers and 58 function and pulse generators, catalogued down to counts of knobs, switches and BNC jacks.
claims.quote_verbatim: he's got 88 multimeters, 38 oscilloscopes, 11 logic analyzers, 58 function pulse gens
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Stored instruments should be powered up periodically, because equipment left unused for long stretches is more likely to fail when it is finally switched on.
claims.quote_verbatim: the reason that this old equipment fails is because if you don't, um, you know, power up and stroke your test instruments once in a while
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: When an established test and measurement service business closes, its warehouse stock of older instruments typically cannot be sold individually and is disposed of by the pallet load or scrapped as electronic waste.
claims.quote_verbatim: You can't sell these onesies, right? You're, you're either going to have to sell them by the pallet load or they're going to have to go to the e-waste.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Liquidations of long-established instrument service companies release warehouses of older equipment, and local enthusiasts strip the highest-value items first so that later buyers see picked-over stock.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's just rows and rows and rows of floor to ceiling warehouse of test equipment
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: On-wafer probing extends to about 750 GHz in dedicated probe rooms, and probes for those frequencies use MEMS contactors that are fragile and can only be repaired by returning them to the manufacturer.
claims.quote_verbatim: we can probe up to 750 gigahertz in our probe room next door to this room
claims.speaker: Greg Charvat
claims.episode_title: The Terahertz Frontier with Greg Charvat of Teradar

claims.claim_text: The most expensive instruments and probes tend to be the most fragile, because performance at extreme frequencies is achieved through delicate mechanical structures with no margin for mishandling.
claims.quote_verbatim: the more expensive the test equipment, the more prone it is to break
claims.speaker: Greg Charvat
claims.episode_title: The Terahertz Frontier with Greg Charvat of Teradar
